title: Chiang Mai in One Day: Old City, Doi Suthep & Nimman
metaDesc: An unhurried one-day Chiang Mai plan: temple-hop the Old City (Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang) in the morning, khao soi for lunch, Doi Suthep in the afternoon, and a chill Nimman evening — with real times, entry fees, and how to get around.
keywords: Chiang Mai one day, Chiang Mai itinerary, Chiang Mai Old City, Doi Suthep, Nimman
h1:
Chiang Mai in One Day
Old City · Doi Suthep · Nimman
intro: Even with just a single day in Chiang Mai you can still pack in a lot, as long as you plan the route well. This itinerary walks you through the Old City temples in the cool morning hours, sends you off for a bowl of khao soi at lunch, takes you up Doi Suthep for the city view in the afternoon, then winds down in the laid-back Nimman area come evening. We've added real times, entry fees, and how to get around — whether you rent a bike, hop on a red songthaew, or grab a Grab.

blocks.html: This plan is built for anyone with a full day to spare — start a little early and you'll fit everything in. The route runs from the Old City (city center) up to Doi Suthep (to the west), then drops back down to finish in Nimman (at the foot of the mountain), which sits right on the way down, so there's no doubling back. The total distance isn't far, but the mountain road winds, so leave yourself a bit of buffer.

blocks.title: How to get around
blocks.html: Renting a car/motorbike is the most flexible option for this plan, especially for the drive up the mountain · Red songthaews can be chartered around town; for Doi Suthep there are pick-up points near the zoo / in front of Rajabhat University, roughly 40–60 THB per person one way (they leave once the truck is full) · Grab is handy in town, but on the way back down the mountain there are few cars and it can be tricky to get one.

blocks.text: Morning — walk the Old City and visit temples

blocks.html: Start your day inside the square moated Old City. In the morning the air is still cool and the crowds haven't arrived, so it's easy to wander, take photos, and visit the temples in peace. Most Old City temples are free to enter (donate as you wish) and open around 6am. Dress modestly — shoulders covered and knees covered, for both men and women.

items.activity: Tha Phae Gate — photos by the red-brick city wall
items.note: The eastern inner city gate and a classic Chiang Mai check-in spot. Early on there are flocks of pigeons and the light is good for photos. Free.

items.activity: Wat Chiang Man — the oldest temple in the city
items.note: A few minutes' walk or ride from Tha Phae. Chiang Mai's very first temple, with an elephant-buttressed chedi and the Crystal Buddha. Rarely crowded.

items.activity: Wat Chedi Luang — the giant chedi in the center of town
items.note: A huge ancient chedi that was once the tallest in the Lanna kingdom. The Inthakhin pillar (city pillar) is housed here. Free.

items.activity: Wat Phra Singh — pay respects to Phra Buddha Sihing
items.note: A major temple of the city. The Lai Kham viharn is beautiful. Open 06:00–18:00, entry to the temple is free; the museum charges around 20–40 THB.

blocks.title: Temple-hopping tips
blocks.html: All three temples are close together within the Old City — you can walk between them in 10–15 minutes per leg. If the sun is fierce that day, renting a bicycle or grabbing a short Grab makes it easier. There are plenty of drink stands and cafés along the way.

blocks.text: Lunch — a bowl of khao soi

blocks.html: You can't come to Chiang Mai and skip khao soi for lunch — egg noodles in a coconut-curry broth made with northern curry paste, topped with crispy fried noodles and eaten with pickled greens and shallots. Most famous shops open in the morning through the afternoon and sell out fast. Head out of the Old City toward Chang Phueak–Fa Ham and you'll find several standout spots — pick one that's on your way before heading up the mountain.

items.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
items.blurb: A long-running shop with a recipe straight from Mae Sai, open for over 20 years and listed in the Michelin Guide. The standouts are the chicken khao soi and the khanom jeen nam ngiao. Plenty of people queue and order through the app, so go before noon.
items.meta: Ratchaphruek Rd, Chang Phueak · Open 09:00–16:00 (closed Sun)

items.name: Khao Soi Lamduan Fa Ham
items.blurb: A Chiang Mai khao soi institution, open for over 70 years, with a rich, well-balanced broth. Both tourists and locals rank it among the very best, and it has several branches.
items.meta: Fa Ham · Near the route out of town

items.name: Khao Soi Samoejai
items.blurb: An old shop of over 30 years next to Wat Fa Ham, with a traditional flavor and a broth fragrant with spices. Chiang Mai locals have been eating here for years. Easygoing, homey atmosphere.
items.meta: Charoenrat Rd, next to Wat Fa Ham · Open 08:00–17:00

items.name: Khao Soi Mae Manee
items.blurb: A longtime Chiang Mai favorite of over 30 years on the Chotana side, worth a stop if you're heading out the north of town. Open morning through afternoon like the others.

blocks.title: Lunch tips
blocks.html: Popular khao soi shops often sell out before the afternoon, so if your morning runs long, have lunch around 11:30–12:00 before heading up the mountain so you don't miss out. While you wait in line, try ordering khanom jeen nam ngiao or sai ua (northern sausage) to snack on.

Once you're full of khao soi, head up Doi Suthep. The road up winds but is well paved, taking about 30–40 minutes from the foot of the mountain. Wat Phra That Doi Suthep is the main destination — a sacred temple of the city perched on the mountaintop, with sweeping views over Chiang Mai on a clear day.

items.note: If you take a red songthaew, board at the pick-up point near the zoo / in front of Rajabhat University, around 40–60 THB per person; they leave once the truck is full.

items.activity: Climb the 306-step Naga staircase, or take the tram
items.note: Walk the Naga staircase for the classic shot; if your legs aren't up to it, there's a tram for around 20 THB.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep — pay respects and take in the view
items.note: Open roughly 06:00–18:00. Entry is 30 THB for foreigners; Thais donate as they wish. The golden chedi and the city viewpoint are the highlights.
A little further up past Doi Suthep, with a lovely flower garden. It's open to visitors only at certain times, so check the opening days before you go. Skip it if you're short on time.

blocks.title: Good to know up the mountain
blocks.html: It's cooler up the mountain than in town, so pack a light jacket · Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, since it's a temple · In the late afternoon clouds can roll in and obscure the view, so go up before 3pm if you want a clear one · Public transport thins out on the way down in the evening, so have a backup plan for getting a ride.

Coming down the mountain drops you right by Nimman. This area sits at the foot of the mountain on the western side of the city, packed with cafés, restaurants, design shops, and community malls — a great place to cap off the day at an easy pace: wander, take photos, sip a coffee, then settle in for dinner.

items.name: One Nimman
items.blurb: A European-style red-brick community mall at the head of Nimman Soi 1, gathering restaurants, cafés, bars, and craft shops. In the evening there are often rotating markets and events, and it's a pleasant place to wander and take photos.

items.name: Nimman cafés
items.blurb: Nimman is café heaven, with stylishly designed shops lining a single soi — northern hill coffee, matcha, and desserts alike. Some stay open into the evening, perfect for resting your legs before dinner.

items.name: Dinner in Nimman
items.blurb: From northern and Thai food to international spots and bars, take your pick. The atmosphere is lively in just the right way in the early evening.

items: 17:00 — Down from the mountain to Nimman, stroll One Nimman and photograph the red-brick architecture
17:30 — Stop at a café for a northern hill coffee or a dessert and rest your legs after a full day
18:30 — Dinner in Nimman; go for northern food or whatever appeals to you
20:00 — Browse the market / event at One Nimman (if there's one that night) to round off the day

blocks.title: If it falls on a Sunday
blocks.html: On Sunday nights there's the walking street running from Wat Phra Singh along Ratchadamnoen in the Old City. If your trip lands on that day, you could swap things around — head back into the Old City in the evening for the walking street instead of Nimman. It's loaded with food and souvenirs.

items: Old City temples — free (Wat Phra Singh museum 20–40 THB)
Transport — songthaew up and down the mountain roughly 80–120 THB, or a motorbike rental around 200–300 THB/day
Food — khao soi for lunch ~60 THB · coffee ~80–120 THB · dinner ~150–300 THB
Total roughly — 500–900 THB per person, not counting accommodation and souvenirs

faq.q: What can you see in Chiang Mai in one day?
faq.a: A route that works well is: morning in the Old City visiting Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang, and Wat Chiang Man; khao soi for lunch; Doi Suthep in the afternoon for the view; and an evening in Nimman to finish. This route avoids doubling back, since Nimman sits right on the way down from the mountain.

faq.q: How much is the entry fee for Doi Suthep?
faq.a: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep charges 30 THB for foreigners; Thais donate as they wish. If you don't want to climb the 306-step Naga staircase, there's a tram up for around 20 THB. The temple is open roughly 06:00–18:00.

faq.q: How do you get up Doi Suthep without your own vehicle?
faq.a: You can take a red songthaew. The pick-up point is near the Chiang Mai Zoo / in front of Rajabhat University, around 40–60 THB per person one way, but they leave only once the truck is full. On the way down in the evening there are few cars, so allow extra time or have Grab as a backup.

faq.q: Where's a good place for khao soi in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Recommended favorites include Khao Soi Mae Sai (Michelin Guide), Khao Soi Lamduan Fa Ham, Khao Soi Samoejai, and Khao Soi Mae Manee. Most are around the Chang Phueak–Fa Ham area, open morning through afternoon and selling out fast, so go before noon.

faq.q: Is it better to go in the morning or the afternoon?
faq.a: Start in the morning — the Old City temples are cooler and quieter early on. As for Doi Suthep, going up before 3pm gives you a clearer city view; on some days clouds roll in late in the afternoon and block it.
